name: Chronic Mucocutaneous Candidiasis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Chronic Mucocutaneous Candidiasis

criteria.description: Recurrent or persistent Candida infections of skin, nails, and mucous membranes lasting more than 6 months
Evidence of impaired cell-mediated immunity against Candida species
Exclusion of other primary or secondary immunodeficiencies causing candidiasis
Identification of mutations in genes such as STAT1, AIRE, or CARD9 associated with CMC

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent Candida infections plus evidence of immune dysfunction and exclusion of other immunodeficiencies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by immunological and genetic testing

pathognomonic.notes: Chronic thrush resistant to standard antifungal therapy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis of skin and nails
pathognomonic.notes: Involves thickened, discolored nails and erythematous plaques

common.notes: Inflammation and cracking at the corners of the mouth

occasional.notes: May be associated in autoimmune polyendocrinopathy syndromes
Seen in autoimmune polyendocrinopathy candidiasis ectodermal dystrophy (APECED)
Due to mucosal involvement or associated autoimmune enteropathy

rare.notes: Rare CNS involvement in severe immunodeficiency

laboratory: Positive cultures for Candida species from mucosal or skin lesions
Impaired T-cell mediated immune response to Candida antigens
Elevated inflammatory markers during active infection
imaging: MRI brain in rare CNS involvement
other: Histopathology showing fungal hyphae invading mucosa

distinguishingFeatures: Profound immunodeficiency with multiple infections beyond Candida
Systemic symptoms and other opportunistic infections
Presence of multiple endocrine autoimmune diseases

redFlags: Persistent or recurrent Candida infections despite antifungal therapy
references: Puel A, et al. Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis disease associated with inborn errors of IL-17 immunity. Science. 2011.
Lionakis MS, et al. STAT1 gain-of-function mutations and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis. J Clin Invest. 2016.
Husebye ES, et al. Autoimmune polyendocrine syndromes. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2018.
